sentences.text: Shri Avinash Sirpurkar Senior Advocate along with Shri   Saxena, learned counsel for the petitioner .
Kshitij Vyas Pl appearing on behalf of Advocate General  ORDER Heard and perused the case diary.

2. This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 658/2023, registered at Police Station-Ranapur, District-Jhabua for the offence under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC 1860.
He is in detention since 24.09.2024.
3. As per prosecution story, it is alleged that the applicant along with co-accused persons has misappropriated the amount of Rs.47.25 lakhs.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted the applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent person and has been falsely implicated.

Another co-accused Jalsingh (against whom the main allegations were levelled) has already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide order NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3296 2 MCRC-55355-2024 dated 18.12.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.49974/2024 subject to payment of Rs.10,00,000/-.
Counsel further submitted that the applicant is also ready to deposit the amount of Rs.5,00,000/- in two installments i.e. each installment of Rs.2,50,000/-.
The applicant is in custody since 24.09.2024.
Trial of the case will Somsingh Ajnar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025

1 take considerable time.

Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
5.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

6. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case and nature of allegation and custody period of the applicant, without expressing any view on merits of the case, I am the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

7. It is directed that subject to deposit of Rs.2,50,000/- by the applicant before the trial Court, the applicant shall be released on bail as well as on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
She shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.

8. After the release of the applicant, second installment of Rs.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3296 3 MCRC-55355-2024 2,50,000/- shall be deposited within a further period of three months from the date of release before the trial Court.
9. It is made clear that in case of single failure to deposit the said amount, this bail order stands vacated automatically without further reference to this Court.

10. This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the preconditions of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified Copy as per rules.
